explanation: Option A is correct because a recursive one-to-many relationship is represented with a self-referential foreign key. Here, manager_id stores the employee_id of another row in the same employees table. Option B duplicates data unnecessarily. Option C does not preserve referential integrity. Option D refers to a managers table that is not part of the stated design.

options.text: Add a manager_id column that references employees.employee_id in the same table
Create a separate managers table and copy every employee into it if they manage someone
Store the manager's name only as text so no foreign key is needed
Use a foreign key from employees.employee_id to managers.manager_id

prompt: A company stores employees in one table: `employees(employee_id, employee_name, manager_id)`. Each employee may have a manager, and the manager is also an employee in the same table. Which design best represents this relationship?
